text: Missus Monarch sat with a stillness. <break time="0.8s" /> That no professional could have equalled. <break time="0.8s" /> Yet, however I arranged her. <break time="0.8s" /> She always came out the same. <break time="0.8s" /> A tall, elegant figure. <break time="0.8s" /> Who looked less like a character. <break time="0.8s" /> Than like a photograph. <break time="0.8s" /> She was the real thing. <break time="0.8s" /> But always the same thing. <break time="0.8s" /> And I came to feel. <break time="0.8s" /> That her very perfection was a kind of prison. <break time="0.8s" /> From which no character in any story could escape. <break time="0.8s" /> The Major was no more useful. <break time="0.8s" /> For, being six feet two. <break time="0.8s" /> And impossible to bend into any other shape. <break time="0.8s" /> He could be employed only. <break time="0.8s" /> For the representation of brawny giants. <break time="0.8s" /> When I asked them to put on costumes. <break time="0.8s" /> They would do so obediently. <break time="0.8s" /> Yet in a borrowed coat or a peasants shawl. <break time="0.8s" /> They somehow looked more like themselves than ever. <break time="0.8s" /> The gentleman and lady stubbornly shining through. <break time="0.8s" /> Miss Churm, by contrast. <break time="0.8s" /> Could put on any role as easily as a hat. <break time="0.8s" /> And the lady in my drawings. <break time="0.8s" /> Though Miss Churm was nothing of the kind. <break time="0.8s" /> Looked more like a lady. <break time="0.8s" /> Than Missus Monarch ever did. <break time="0.8s" /> The truth. <break time="0.8s" /> Which I had always half known. <break time="0.8s" /> Now became painfully plain. <break time="0.8s" /> Namely that I had an innate preference. <break time="0.8s" /> For the represented subject over the real one. <break time="0.8s" /> Since the defect of the real one. <break time="0.8s" /> Was so often a lack of representation. <break time="0.8s" /> Only then did I understand. <break time="0.8s" /> Why my best ladies had always been drawn. <break time="0.8s" /> From a girl who was not a lady at all. <break time="0.8s" /> For an artist needs not what is but what can be imagined. <break time="0.8s" /> Yet I could not bring myself. <break time="0.8s" /> To send the Monarchs away. <break time="0.8s" /> So patient were they. <break time="0.8s" /> So eager to please. <break time="0.8s" /> And so quietly anxious every morning. <break time="0.8s" /> When they climbed the stairs to my studio.
